feature: Copy, cut and paste a range of time
summary: With a range drawn on the ruler, Cmd-C copies that stretch of every track, Cmd-X copies it and closes the gap, and Cmd-V lays it in at the playhead on the same tracks, covering what was there.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording, drop a second clip on V1 so there is a cut to copy across.

try.do: Drag along the ruler from 0:05 to 0:09 to draw a range, then press Cmd-C.
Click the ruler at 0:12 and press Cmd-V.
Press Space from the start and watch both copies play.
Press Cmd-Z once: the whole paste goes.
Draw the same range again and press Cmd-X.
Right-click inside a range on the ruler: Cut and Copy sit above Delete.
Right-click the ruler anywhere and choose Paste to lay the copy in there.

evaluate: Is it right that the playhead jumps to the end of what you pasted, so a second Cmd-V follows straight on?
Is it right that what you pasted is picked afterwards?
Should Cmd-V cover what is under it (as now), or push it along the way Premiere's Shift-Cmd-V does?
Would you expect Cmd-C to copy a range you set with I and O, not only one you dragged on the ruler?
rough: Cmd-C and Cmd-X only take the range while it is in hand (just drawn, nothing else picked). Marks set with I and O copy from the right-click only.
There is no insert paste (Shift-Cmd-V) yet: every paste covers what is under it.
A range copied in one window will not paste into another; Cmd-V there pastes what it always did.
A range on just some tracks (Option-drag on the tracks) is not copied yet; Cmd-C with one in hand copies the picked layer as before.
Clips on a locked track are left out of the copy, the same way Delete leaves them.
Nothing on screen says a copy was made: the timeline does not change, as in Final Cut.
